gaps.sentence: She ___ attention to every detail of the contract.
She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: I only ___ sight of the celebrity for a second before the crowd closed in.
gaps.explanation: catch sight of somebody/something means to notice them briefly.

gaps.sentence: I would never ___ advice from someone I don't respect.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'advice' from the receiver's side
gaps.explanation: take advice from somebody means to accept and follow it; the adviser gives advice.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune selling software online.
gaps.explanation: make a fortune means to earn a very large amount of money.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: Try to ___ quiet — the exam is in progress.
gaps.explanation: keep quiet means to stay silent; 'make quiet' is not used.

gaps.sentence: Could you ___ me a favour and close the window?
gaps.explanation: do somebody a favour is the fixed collocation; 'make a favour' is a common error.
